```{r loading-library}

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(kableExtra)
library(broom)
```

```{r reading-data}
#| include: false

airquality_data <- read_csv(here("data/air_quality.csv"))
```

```{r tidying-data}
#| include: false

airquality_data<- airquality_data |> 
  mutate(
    month = month(date, label = TRUE, abbr= TRUE),
    year = as.factor(year(date))
  )
```

## Problem Introduction

::: columns

::: {.column width="60%"}
- Air pollution is a major public health issue causing respiratory problems leading to increased hospital admissions
- We will explore data on air pollution levels and hospital admissions in 8 major cities across 2020–2025
- This presentation will examine how air pollution has affected hospital intakes in the most polluted cities in the years 2020-2025

:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![Credit: Thoracic and Sleep Group](air-polution-illustration.png){width="100%"}
:::

:::

## Dataset Exploration

- The dataset contained daily air quality and healthcare observations from eight cities between 2020 and 2025. 

- Key variables included: `Air Quality Index (AQI)`, `PM2.5`, `PM10`, `NO2`, `O3`, `temperature`, `humidity`, `hospital admissions`, and `hospital capacity`. 

- Daily observations were aggregated into monthly summaries and then yearly summaries to reduce short-term fluctuations and improve trend interpretation.

## Methodology

The analysis was conducted using R and several packages from the `tidyverse` [@R-tidyverse] ecosystem for data cleaning, transformation, modelling, and visualisation. 

The following ibraries were used for date handling, plotting, table formatting, and regression analysis:

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}

- `lubridate` [@R-lubridate] for date manipulation

- `ggplot2` [@R-ggplot2] for data visualisation

- `patchwork` [@R-patchwork] for combining multiple plots

- `kableExtra` [@R-kableExtra] for enhanced table formatting

- `broom` [@R-broom] for tidying regression outputs

- `here` [@R-here] for reproducible file paths

:::
